mermaid:
flowchart TD
  subgraph GUI["Application"]
    G1["src/main.rs"]
    G2["src/ui/app.rs"]
    G3["src/terminal/view.rs"]
  end
  subgraph CORE["Coeur"]
    C1["crates/tty7-core/src/client/mod.rs"]
    C2["crates/tty7-core/src/daemon/protocol.rs"]
    C3["crates/tty7-core/src/daemon/server.rs"]
    C4["crates/tty7-core/src/daemon/pane.rs"]
  end
  subgraph CLI["CLI et mobile"]
    L1["crates/tty7-cli/src/main.rs"]
    L2["crates/tty7-gateway/src/serve.rs"]
  end
  G1 --> G2
  G2 --> G3
  G3 --> C1
  L1 --> C1
  L2 --> C1
  C1 --> C2
  C2 --> C3
  C3 --> C4
explication: La fenêtre graphique, la CLI et la passerelle mobile parlent au même démon via le client du coeur. Le serveur du démon possède les panes et leurs shells, ce qui permet aux sessions de survivre à la fermeture de l'application.
source: Claude, d'après l'arbre du dépôt et le README
explication_en: The graphical window, the CLI and the mobile gateway talk to the same daemon through the core client. The daemon server owns the panes and their shells, which lets sessions survive the application being closed.
